newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-BEVAN AND DALE EQUAL LAST WICKET RECORD STAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BEVAN AND DALE EQUAL LAST WICKET RECORD STAND.

text.p: A record-equalling last-wicket stand of 45 spared Australia's blushes as they made 223 for nine off their 50 overs in the first one-day match against South Africa on Saturday.

Michael Bevan (51 not out) and fast bowler Adam Dale, making his international debut, equalled the Australian 10th wicket limited overs record of 45 by Trevor Laughlin and Max Walker against England at Sydney in 1979-80.
Tigerish fielding from South Africa had contributed to a collapse in which seven wickets tumbled for 49, leaving the touring team on 178 for nine.
Stuart Law and Steve Waugh had earlier both made exactly 50 during a third-wicket stand of 97 that seemed to have laid the platform for a large total at 129 for two.
But they were dismissed within 10 deliveries of each other and the rot set in.
Law pulled off-spinner Pat Symcox to deep mid-wicket after reaching his seventh half-century in his 38th match from 65 deliveries, with six fours.
New batsman Greg Blewett then called Waugh for a quick single to Jonty Rhodes and was stranded a yard short of his crease by a direct hit.
Waugh's 27th 50 in his 212th match came from 61 balls and contained four boundaries.
Blewett (14) was run out by a direct hit from Hansie Cronje at long-on and Rhodes struck a third time with yet another direct hit that saw wicketkeeper Adam Gilchrist (1) run out by about five yards.

But Bevan reached his 10th half-century in his 50th one-day international from just 57 balls, with three fours and a six, and Dale showed he will not be batting at number 11 for long as he made 15 not out on a slow but blameless surface.
Mark Waugh was replaced in Australia's team just before the start by Tasmanian Michael DiVenuto, making his debut. Waugh had a stiff and sore back.
There are seven one-day games in the series.
